data.body: Patchset-1 CI RCA (run 31773167187): the fixture schema stores exactly one `pandoc.binary_sha256`, generated on macOS arm64 (`94ebf1efbce3561379e8f25de3efe5aeabee64dc36dd8e8b9e96cf05b4195c52`). Runtime logs from all three Ubuntu jobs (Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13) observed the same pinned Pandoc 3.6.1 Linux x86_64 binary hash (`4715627586c5d9c732e8f5a6b6bb9e27c4216a76a7729e043b24374dedf8a1f0`) and rejected it solely against the macOS hash; macOS-26-arm64 accepted the fixture. Thus the changeable defect is the single-platform provenance object emitted at scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:153-157 and compared wholesale at tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py:452-462. It models a platform-specific binary fingerprint as platform-independent. Pandoc version and the 884 output comparisons otherwise agree, ruling out version drift or output incompatibility. Defect legitimacy: the reviewed acceptance contract requires exact generating version plus SHA-256 and CI supports both macOS arm64 and Ubuntu x86_64; weakening to version-only is prohibited. Expected repair: retain generating platform/fingerprint, add the exact supported-platform fingerprint map, select by stable platform/architecture, reject unknown platforms and version/hash mismatches, and preserve the complete map during deterministic regeneration. Caller sweep: this schema is consumed only by the generator tests and hardening test; no production/library caller behavior depends on the single-hash shape.
